prompt: Use case: illustration-story. A single landscape 3:2 illustration for the historical atlas sketchbook of Jules Verne's Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea. A nineteenth-century naturalist's field sketch in graphite and sepia pen with restrained transparent watercolour washes on warm ivory paper. Fine irregular parallel hatching, economical contour lines, a few details sharply observed; leave areas of cream paper around irregular unfinished edges. One coherent scene that reads at small sizes. No captions, labels, border, binding, signatures, photorealism, modern equipment, or Disney submarine designs. At a timber wharf in Brooklyn in 1867, people stand close together watching a large dark steam frigate ease out into New York harbour. Three sailing masts and one smoking funnel, tug and small spectator boats distant, period jackets and bonnets, no modern bridge, skyscrapers or Statue of Liberty. Low view along the planks past the cast-off mooring line toward the departing ship.
